CAZ
A locator — a coordinate on model depth that
brackets where a concept is assembled.
Operationally, a scored saddle-to-saddle segment
of the separation curve (§4.3); not the concept,
and not a functional module
CAZ Profile
The full sequence of CAZes for one concept in
one model
Major CAZ
CAZ with score > 0.5 — the highest
composite-salience band; score reflects
prominence, coherence, and width jointly (§4.3),
not spatial narrowness — a Major CAZ can
span an entire network
Strong CAZ
CAZ with 0.2 < score ≤0.5
Moderate CAZ
CAZ with 0.05 < score ≤0.2
Gentle CAZ
A low-salience CAZ (score < 0.05), invisible to
standard peak detection; the validation paper
finds these regions causally active under
geometric ablation in most cases (§7) — a direct
illustration that the score grades salience, not
causal importance
Embedding CAZ
CAZ at the earliest stored (transformer-block)
layers, driven by near-lexical/token-level
features rather than deep computation. The
pre-transformer embedding output is excluded
from extraction, so this denotes the earliest
block layers, not the raw embedding (see §4.1)
Active CAZ
CAZ within the transformer layers, driven by
attention and MLP computation. Active CAZes
are the primary subject of this framework
CAZ score
Composite metric: (prominence / mean
separation) × coherence boost ×

width/N
(full form in §4.3)
Separation S(l)
Within-class-scale-normalized centroid distance
between contrastive classes at layer l
Coherence C(l)
Explained variance ratio of the primary
separating direction at layer l
Velocity v(l)
Smoothed rate of change of S(l) across layers
Directional Stability DS(l)
Layer-to-layer cosine similarity of the dominant
concept direction ˆd(l); near 1.0 means the
direction barely moved; a sharp drop marks a
handoff event (§4.2)
